newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran vows to hold rally at Moslem pilgrimage.
newsitem.headline: Iran vows to hold rally at Moslem pilgrimage.

text.p: Iran vowed on Monday that its pilgrims would defy a Saudi ban and hold a rally to denounce the United States and Israel at the Moslem haj pilgrimage in Saudi Arabia in April, state-run Tehran radio said.

It quoted Iran's haj supervisor Mohammad Mohammadi Reyshahri as saying: "The disavowal of infidels is the high point of the social goals of haj...We should try with all our power to perform the true haj as revealed to us by the late Imam (Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini)."
He was referring to the rally which radical Shi'ite Iran says should be held as part of the annual pilgrimage to denounce the enemies of Islam.
Saudi Arabia'a conservative Sunni rulers say haj is a purely religious affair and should not be politicised. Riyadh has banned all political activities during haj in the past years.
Saudi security forces clashed in 1987 with demonstrators in an Iranian-led rally in the streets of Mecca, killing about 400 people, mainly Iranians.

Iran boycotted the haj for the next three years. There has been no repeat of the bloodshed since the return of Iranian pilgrims in 1991 and their haj rallies have been low-key affairs often confined to the Iranian compounds.
Saudi Arabia recently warned pilgrims they would face tough punishment if they carried political material to haj, which draws up to two million Moslems from across the world.
